camps.name: Westwater campground
camps.desc: At the put-in. Sites 1 to 7 are first come, first served, $20 a night, along the river; sites 8 to 11 and a group site for up to 30 are reserved on Recreation.gov.

camps.name: Miners Camp
camps.desc: A large camp with 4WD roads and washes for hiking into the desert. About halfway through the upper flatwater.

camps.name: Upper Cougar Bar
camps.desc: A large camp with a small sandy beach.

camps.name: Lower Cougar Bar
camps.desc: A small camp usable at low water only. A wash leads uphill to an overlook of the Little Dolores River.

camps.name: Little Hole
camps.desc: A large camp across from Little Hole. Ferry across to hike the petroglyphs.

camps.name: Upper Little Dolores
camps.desc: A large, popular camp with hikes up the Little Dolores, a spring waterfall, and eddy service to the Little D surf wave.

camps.name: Lower Little Dolores
camps.desc: A second large, popular camp. At low and medium water you carry gear across a brushy cobble bar and up a hill.

camps.name: Hades Bar
camps.desc: A small camp with a rocky beach.

camps.name: Big Hole
camps.desc: Good for exploring on foot but with very little room.

camps.name: Big Horn
camps.desc: A large camp with rock walls on both sides of a beach.

camps.name: Bald Eagle
camps.desc: A large camp with a nice beach.

rapids.name: Little Wild Horse Rapids
rapids.desc: Several small rapids between miles 3.7 and 4.9, a warm-up for the canyon.

rapids.name: Wild Horse Rapids
rapids.desc: A cobble stretch; some rock-dodging at low water.

rapids.name: Little Dolores Rapids
rapids.desc: A two-part rapid at the Little Dolores confluence, with a large hole center right that is easy to avoid but hard to recognize. A good kayak play wave in the second half.

rapids.name: Marble Canyon Rapids
rapids.desc: The first significant canyon rapid: a long wave train with a left bend, fun down the right side.

rapids.name: Staircase Rapids
rapids.desc: Reported line: run left of center.

rapids.name: Big Hummer Rapids
rapids.desc: Reported line: run right of center.

rapids.name: Funnel Falls
rapids.desc: The first rapid of the main gorge, formed by two boulders. Run left, center or right depending on the water level; most challenging at high water.

rapids.name: Surprise Rapids
rapids.desc: Two parts, mostly two steep wave trains.

rapids.name: Skull Rapid
rapids.desc: The most consequential rapid, with a boulder jumble on the left, a steep wall on the right and a distinct horizon line; a small eddy to scout. Below about 4,000 cfs a large center rock forces a squeeze between rock and wall; above that, run center to left, and don't pull left too early. At medium to high flow the center forms a large hole that has flipped rafts. Room of Doom, a circling eddy on river right, can trap boats above about 6,000 cfs and has no exit above 10,000.

rapids.name: Bowling Alley
rapids.desc: A wave train. Follow it down the middle.

rapids.name: Sock It To Me
rapids.desc: The largest wave train in the canyon, with a meaty wave-hole. It angles right to left, so start from the right and hit the entrance hard and straight, then pull right to avoid the wall.

rapids.name: Last Chance Rapid
rapids.desc: A boulder in the center splits the channel. At 3,000 to 4,000 cfs left and right both work, the right steep and bumpy. The last rapid in the canyon.

hikes.name: Miner's cabin
hikes.desc: A small cabin reached by a short hike. Look but do not touch.

hikes.name: Little Hole petroglyphs
hikes.desc: Ferry across from Little Hole Camp.

hikes.name: Little Dolores River
hikes.desc: Hike upstream from Upper Little Dolores Camp to a spring waterfall about three quarters of a mile up.

hikes.name: Outlaw Cave
hikes.desc: A small cave, once the home of two outlaws, with historical artifacts. Do not touch.

hikes.name: Schist canyon exit hike
hikes.desc: A short hike out of the schist canyon for a view of the canyon within a canyon.

flows: The river peaks around 20,000 cfs in late May or early June and recedes to about 3,000 cfs in the fall.
A high-water trip above 10,000 cfs can take 4 hours; at 1,000 to 5,000 cfs it can take 10 or more.
Between 13,000 and 20,000 cfs the main canyon is serious Class IV with few eddies between rapids, and a swim or flip can last miles.
geology: The canyon is cut through 1.7-billion-year-old Vishnu Schist, rock that also appears in Ruby-Horsethief and the Grand Canyon.
indigenous: Petroglyphs near Little Hole record a long human presence in the canyon, in country long used by the Ute people and by earlier groups before them. Look, photograph and leave the panels untouched.
history: Cisco began in the 1880s as a saloon and water stop on the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad. Over 100,000 sheep were sheared there around the turn of the 20th century before shipping to market. Oil and gas were found in 1924, but the town declined with the end of steam locomotives and was bypassed by Interstate 70. Its ruins were used for scenes in the 1971 film Vanishing Point.
The Westwater valley and Cisco were stops for water, wood and grass along the North Branch of the Old Spanish Trail before the railroad came.
Stories tell of two outlaw brothers who lived in the cave above the river and left artifacts behind. Do not touch or take anything from the site.

rules.d: A first aid kit, a repair kit, an air pump, and a washable, leak-proof, reusable toilet system. Wag bags must be in a hard-sided, clamped or screw-top container.
All fires must be in a fire pan at least 12 inches in diameter with a 1.5 inch lip. A fire blanket and ash container are recommended.
A properly sized Type I, III or V life jacket for each person. Life jackets are required from the ranger station to Big Hole, and children 12 and under must wear one at all times.

Each raft, dory or canoe needs an extra oar or paddle and a bail bucket or bilge pump unless self-bailing. Every boat needs a whistle. Boats 16 feet or longer need a throwable and a throw bag with at least 40 feet of line.
Parties of kayaks, inflatable kayaks or SUPs carry one spare paddle for every three vessels.
Trips must launch, travel within visual contact, and camp together from the ranger station to Cisco.
One overnight is allowed, on your launch date only, at the site the ranger assigns. Groups launching separately may not camp together if the site would hold more than 25.
Launch only from the Westwater Ranger Station, once per day. Boat tags must stay attached.
Gather only driftwood from banks and beaches.
No dogs in the canyon. Drones are prohibited.
Carry out all trash, ash and charcoal, and solid human and service dog waste. Keep side canyon streams and springs free of soap.
Camping is not authorized for two river miles below Cisco Landing, and motors are not allowed below it for two miles. Use the far river-right channel around the large island below the landing.
Bring all your drinking water, at least a gallon per person per day.
There is no cell coverage in the canyon.
Call 911. The Grand County Sheriff leads search and rescue.
Burned slopes in the upper Little Dolores increase flash flood and debris flow risk. Check the weather before camping or hiking nearby.

landmarks.name: Westwater Ranger Station
landmarks.desc: Put-in with a boat ramp, campground, pit toilets and trash and recycling. Check in with the ranger for a campsite assignment.

landmarks.name: Good Luck Wall
landmarks.desc: A large cliff face coming straight down to the river on the right. Tradition is to touch it for luck.

landmarks.name: Little Dolores River
landmarks.desc: The Little Dolores enters on the left. The last campsites above the rapids.

landmarks.name: Cliff hole
landmarks.desc: A large hole in the cliff face on river right near the take-out, a popular bouldering problem.

landmarks.name: Cisco boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Take-out with a three-lane concrete ramp, pit toilets, dumpsters and overnight parking. Fish Ford, 5 miles farther, is an optional lower take-out.

notes.camp: *The ranger assigns your single overnight camp when you check in. Side-canyon camps can flood in a storm, so camp on high ground.
notes.hike: *Ferry carefully to reach hikes across the river, and tie up boats well. Look at petroglyphs and historic sites but never touch them.

access.name: Moab
access.note: BLM Moab Field Office and shuttle base

items.d: Private permits open on Recreation.gov two months before the launch date at 8 a.m. Mountain. Any open date can be reserved until 11:59 a.m. on the launch day.
Permits can be printed starting 14 days before launch. No changes are allowed after printing.
At the Westwater Ranger Station a ranger checks your permit and equipment and assigns a campsite. If no ranger is on duty, self-register at the kiosk by the boat ramp.
No permits are issued at the ranger station.
$10 per person, plus a non-refundable $6 reservation fee.
Up to 25 people per permit. Private use is limited to five permits or 75 people per day.
Permit holders must be 18 or older. Permits are for private, non-commercial use and are not transferable. One person may hold up to three permits at a time.
Cancellations or group size reductions more than 14 days before launch are refunded, minus the $6 fee. No refund within 14 days of launch.
Group size can be changed up to 25, if quota allows, until 11:59 a.m. on launch day. Trips can switch between day and overnight if space allows. The alternate trip leader cannot be changed.

stats.season: Year-round. The river peaks near 20,000 cfs in late May or early June and recedes below 3,000 in fall.

flow.note: Runnable from about 2,000 to 30,000 cfs. Between 13,000 and 20,000 the canyon is serious Class IV, and above about 6,000 the eddy fences get hard for rafts.
